newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania OTC market up, high-caps on the rise.
newsitem.headline: Romania OTC market up, high-caps on the rise.

text.p: Romania's over-the-counter (OTC) market ended on a positive note on Monday, when most prices drifted up under strong buying pressure.
"There was a true rally today and I see it continuing at the next session," a trader said, adding that he expected investors to keep their focus on the oil and steel sectors.
Advancers outnumbered losers by 105 to 80, while 420 stocks ended flat.

The unofficial index VAB-RA, computed by Vanguard securities, went up by 10.4 percent to 4,058 points, while the BIG-OTC, compiled by the BIG brokerage house, surged by 15.75 percent to 3,046.83 Another independent index, CAS-RQ, by Creditanstalt Securities, was up 15.83 percent to 699 points.
All three indices are based on average prices and market capitalisation.

Oil refineries were in demand, with Petromidia snatching centre-stage. The refinery closed 7,000 lei firmer at 30,000 after what traders called speculative play throughout the session. "There was profit-taking for most of the day, but Petromidia recovered in late trading," one said.
Another refinery Arpechim ended 1,000 lei up at 27,500.
Steel mill Otelinox firmed 1,500 lei to 34,500, mainly on the back of a special deal involving 200,000 shares traded at 35,000 lei per share.
Traders said there had been special deals also in several small-caps.
"Pressure on Otelinox was high, with investors determined to buy shares before the price went up after selloff of a majority stake," a broker said.
The State Ownership Fund, which has a control stake in most Romanian companies, plans to sell 51 percent of Otelinox to a strategic foreign investor.
Another steel mill, Sidex, gained 900 lei at close to 16,400 in heavy demand.
Turnover fell to 24.6 billion lei from 37.3 billion on Friday
